title: Private deployment DR & Backup/Restore playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft playbook for disaster recovery (DR) and backup/restore for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Target audience: SREs, platform engineers, solutions engineers running customer installs, and customers who operate in air-gapped/private mode. The goal is pragmatic: document what to back up, how to restore, terraform considerations (state, modules), and a tested upgrade + rollback checklist that ties into DR drills.

Status / caveats:
- Drafted during Q1 planning; assumes current runtime architecture (2025 runtime).
- Many two-line TODOs below marked with [ACTION].
- This doc mixes operational runbook steps and design notes. Move final runbook steps to the Console runbooks repo once stabilized.

Definitions / targets:
- RTO objective (target): 30 minutes for control-plane restoration in most outage classes; 2 hours for full inference + console in on-prem single-region installs.
- RPO objective (target): 1 hour for metadata/DB; model artifacts can be restored from object storage snapshots up to 24 hours old depending on customer SLA.
- Scope: covers etcd/metadata DB (Postgres), object storage (S3-compatible), model artifact storage (weights), KV caches (ephemeral, not backed up), Vault/Secrets (integrations), Terraform state for infra.

High-level recovery strategy:
1) Failover vs rebuild: For VPC deployments with multi-AZ, prefer failover using replicated DB + object storage replication. For single-site on-prem, prefer immutable rebuild from snapshots + terraform apply + restore DB snapshots.
2) Source-of-truth: Postgres (metadata) + Terraform remote state. We treat object storage as the single durable copy for artifacts.
3) Secrets: Customer-managed KMS/HSM + HashiCorp Vault (or cloud KMS). Back up only the minimum (unseal keys, policies); do not store plaintext secrets in backups.

What to back up (priority order):
- Postgres logical backups (pg_dump) and base backups (pg_basebackup) for physical restore. Prefer WAL archiving to support PITR.
- Terraform state files (remote state snapshots + periodic versioned backups). Locking + encryption required.
- Object storage buckets containing model weights, optimized kernels, quantized artifacts, and custom model registry entries.
- Vault unseal keys and core ACL policies (encrypted backups).
- Deployment manifests and config (Helm charts, k8s manifests or Docker Compose files) stored in git; snapshot git repo at release times.
- Node-level VM images (golden images) where used for deterministic rebuilds.
- Logs and tracing indices (short retention in primary, longer retention offsite for audits).

Backup frequency and retention recommendations (starter defaults):
- Postgres WAL: archive continuously, keep 7 days of WAL segments (increase for high-risk customers).
- Logical pg_dump: daily at 02:00 local op-time; retained 14 days.
- Object storage: daily incremental snapshot + weekly full snapshot; keep 30 days for incremental and 90 days for full with offsite copy.
- Terraform state: push to remote state (S3/GCS + Dynamo/Lock table) and snapshot on every terraform apply; keep last 50 versions.
- Vault backups: daily encrypted backup; store offsite and rotate unseal key escrow every quarter.

Backup mediums and options:
- S3-compatible object storage (minio for on-prem) with lifecycle rules and cross-region replication for hosted-like installs.
- Tape/air-gapped export for extremely regulated customers (documented but manual).
- Remote state backends: S3/GCS/Azure blob with state lock table (Dynamo/consul) recommended. Local file state: unacceptable for production.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- Remote state: require backend configuration in customer modules; add automated snapshotting wrapper in module releases (module should call a CI job to tag remote state snapshot post-apply).
- State locking: require DynamoDB or Consul for lock; include TTL and retry policies in provider docs.
- Module idempotency: modules must be re-entrant; avoid generating dynamic names that break restores. Use predictable names with suffixes defined by variables.
- Drift recovery: add a "reconcile" make target that runs terraform plan/apply in dry-run mode to detect drift and optional auto-fix.
- Sensitive outputs: minimize terraform outputs; secrets should be read from Vault not exported to state. If outputs are necessary, encrypt them (SOPS) and store in a protected bucket.
- Example terraform restore flow:
  a) Restore remote state snapshot into [restore-state-bucket] with version tag restore-TIMESTAMP.
  b) Configure backend to point at restore bucket with a new workspace name.
  c) Run terraform plan to observe proposed changes — this should be a no-op if state restored correctly.
  d) terraform apply with -refresh=true to reconcile any small drift.
  e) Re-enable CI pipelines to use restored workspace.

Upgrade + DR interplay notes:
- Upgrades modify DB schema and artifact layouts. Always capture DB backup and remote-state snapshot before upgrades.
- For major runtime upgrades (breaking DB migrations), use blue/green or canary strategy: apply schema migration to read-only replica first, run data migration tests against test snapshot, then cut over.
- Keep a matrix of upgrade compatibility: runtime version -> supported DB schema version -> rollback window. Store matrix in Confluence linked_artifacts.

Restore runbook (high-level):
1) Triage and classify event (disk failure, catastrophe, ransomware, config corruption).
2) If data corruption suspected, snapshot current volumes immediately and isolate network access.
3) Restore Postgres:
   - If PITR available: restore base backup + apply WAL up to recovery_target_time.
   - Else: restore latest logical dump and reapply missing transactions if available.
   - Run integrity checks (row counts, sample queries against key tables: deployments, models, routes).
4) Restore object storage:
   - For S3: copy objects from replicated region or restore from versioned snapshots.
   - For minio: use mc mirror from backup bucket to active cluster.
5) Restore terraform state and reapply infra changes: follow terraform restore flow above.
6) Restore Vault: unseal and apply policies; rotate credentials that may have been leaked during incident.
7) Start services in order: DB -> object store -> control plane -> worker nodes -> inference endpoints.
8) Smoke tests: token-generation sanity checks, model load test (small), auth checks, and telemetry ingestion verification.
9) Postmortem timeline capture and customer notification template (link in linked_artifacts).

Commands & snippets (examples, adapt per install):
- Postgres base backup (physical): 
  PGPASSFILE=/etc/postgresql/.pgpass pg_basebackup -h pg-primary -D /var/lib/pgdata/base -U repl -F tar -z -P
- WAL archiving (example wal-e style): 
  wal-e backup-push /var/lib/postgresql/data
- Logical dump daily (cron): 
  PGPASSFILE=/etc/postgresql/.pgpass pg_dump -Fc -f /backups/pgdump-$(date +%F).dump redwooddb
- Minio sync restore: 
  mc mirror --remove backup/minio/model-artifacts/ active/minio/model-artifacts/
- Terraform restore (skeleton): 
  export TF_BACKEND_BUCKET=restore-state-bucket
  aws s3 cp s3://$TF_BACKEND_BUCKET/snapshots/restore-TIMESTAMP/state.tfstate ./terraform.tfstate
  terraform init -reconfigure
  terraform plan -out=plan.restore
  terraform apply plan.restore

Verification checklist after restore (minimal):
- Control plane API responds to /healthz and /ready endpoints.
- Recently restored DB has expected schema version (check migration table).
- Model registry lists expected model ids; sample GET model metadata returns valid checksum.
- Deploy a smoke test model: run generation for predefined prompts and verify tokens returned and latency within expected band.
- Vault secrets unlock and rotate keys; confirm application secrets fetched successfully.
- Console dashboard metrics show ingestion and no sustained 5xx errors.

Test plan and DR drills:
- Quarterly tabletop exercise for engineers + weekly on-call drill for synthetic restores in staging.
- Biannual full restore from cold backups into an isolated cluster (preferably in a different network/region).
- Runbook verification: test the documented commands during each drill and update scripts if commands change.
- Drill metrics: total restore elapsed time, RPO achieved, number of manual fixes required.

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- Terraform state corruption: mitigation = restore snapshot, lock workspace, rerun plan. Add CI gating to detect destructive outputs.
- WAL backlog too large for PITR window: mitigation = increase WAL retention and/or take more frequent base backups.
- Object-store partial replication: mitigation = verify checksums after replication job; have out-of-band archive.
- Vault lock/unseal failures: keep a secure escape hatch for escrowed unseal keys and document HSM recovery steps.

Post-restore hardening & follow-up actions:
- Rotate keys/secrets and rotate TLS certs if leak suspected.
- Increase audit log retention temporarily.
- Conduct blameless postmortem: timeline + contributing factors + 3 action items with owners and target dates.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- [ACTION] Define SLO-based RTO/RPO per-customer plan in pricing matrix (ops and sales to agree).
- [ACTION] Automate terraform state snapshotting as a CI/CD job (owner: infra team).
- [ACTION] Add automated integration test that provisions a minimal private deployment from terraform, injects test data, backs up, destroys, and restores into a new namespace to validate backups. (owner: solutions-engineering)
- [QUESTION] For air-gapped installs, how do we validate object storage snapshots offline without exposing keys? Proposal: signed manifest with checksums stored on removable media.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- GitHub terraform modules: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-terraform/tree/main/modules
- Vault backup guide (internal): CONFLUENCE-VAULT-BACKUP-879
- Upgrade compatibility matrix: CONFLUENCE-UPGRADES-569
- Incident notification template: CONFLUENCE-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE-22

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this file as the canonical draft until infra module has the snapshot wrapper. Move final to /shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/runbooks when approved.
- Pair with Priya on the DR drill checklist; schedule first full restore for staging next month.

End of draft playbook.
